description: If the current app is available, use its json.dumps method for serialization; otherwise, fallback to json.dumps from the standard json module.
If the current app is available, use its json.dump method to serialize and write to a file; otherwise, fallback to json.dump from the standard json module.
If the current app is available, use its json.loads method for deserialization; otherwise, fallback to json.loads from the standard json module.
If the current app is available, use its json.load method to deserialize data from a file; otherwise, fallback to json.load from the standard json module.
Serialize the given arguments as JSON and return a flask.Response object with the application/json mimetype. This operation requires an active app context.
The data must be a string or UTF-8 bytes when using the loads method.
Writing to a file must use text mode with UTF-8 encoding to be valid JSON when using the dump method.
The load method requires the file to be opened in text mode or binary mode with UTF-8 bytes for deserialization.
The application must have a `static_folder` defined to serve static files correctly.
The application can only be run using `app.run()` if it has not been invoked from Flask's command line interface to avoid blocking CLI commands.
The configuration for `SERVER_NAME` must be explicitly set to enable subdomain routing and must not depend on default values.
The return value from request handlers must be a valid response type: either a string, bytes, dict, list, tuple, or a response object.
If `max_age` is set to None, the browser should utilize conditional requests instead of a timed cache to optimize resource retrieval.
If any registered `before_request` handler returns a non-None value, request processing must terminate immediately with that return value.

Exceptions raised by view functions will not propagate if `PROPAGATE_EXCEPTIONS` is set to False and the application is not in debug mode, preventing the default behavior of outputting error details to the client.
View functions must not return None or types that are not recognized as valid response objects (such as plain strings or unsupported types) to ensure a consistent response structure.
When in debug mode, Flask will present a complete stack trace of exceptions that occur during request handling for enhanced debugging capability.
The application must load `.env` and `.flaskenv` files to set environment variables when the `load_dotenv` option is enabled with a value of True.
The application requires that `SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY` configuration parameter is set to True to enhance security by preventing access to cookies from client-side scripts.
The application will only serve static files if `static_folder` is correctly defined and configured, ensuring proper handling of static resources.
All request teardown functions will be executed regardless of whether an exception was encountered during the request, ensuring cleanup actions are consistently performed.
Any errors that occur during the request teardown will be collected and raised if encountered, ensuring that exceptions are properly managed and reported.
The application must raise an error if `make_response` is provided with an invalid response type from a view function, ensuring response validity.
URLs generated through the `url_for` function may include an anchor if it is provided through the `_anchor` argument in order to facilitate navigation to specific sections of a page.
The application must automatically provide options responses if `provide_automatic_options` is set to True and the request method is OPTIONS to streamline method discovery compliance.
The application must validate the consistency between `static_host` and `host_matching` when adding a static route to ensure proper routing behavior.
The 'static_folder' must be set to serve static files; otherwise, a RuntimeError is raised.
Resources can only be opened for reading; valid modes are 'r', 'rt', and 'rb'.
The default configuration for SEND_FILE_MAX_AGE_DEFAULT is None, which tells the browser to use conditional requests instead of a timed cache.
If SEND_FILE_MAX_AGE_DEFAULT is set, its value should be returned in seconds when it is a timedelta; otherwise, None should be returned.
If SEND_FILE_MAX_AGE_DEFAULT is an integer, it should be returned directly without further modifications.
A Flask application must be specified using the '--app' option, the 'FLASK_APP' environment variable, or by having a 'wsgi.py' or 'app.py' file in the current directory.
If multiple Flask applications are detected in a module, a NoAppException will be raised, requiring the user to specify the correct one explicitly.
A factory function for creating a Flask application must be callable without arguments; if it cannot be called as such, a NoAppException is raised.
If the specified application name does not correspond to a valid attribute name or a valid function call, a NoAppException will be raised.
The environment variable 'FLASK_DEBUG' controls whether the application runs in debug mode. If not set, debug mode defaults to 'False'.
If the debug option is not explicitly set during command execution, it will default to the current value of the 'FLASK_DEBUG' environment variable.
The command to launch the development server ('run') is intended solely for development purposes; it is not suitable for production environments.
The command 'routes' displays all registered routes in the application, along with their associated methods and endpoints.
A command will always execute within the application's app context when using the decorator 'with_appcontext'.
When using SSL, if the '--key' option is provided, the '--cert' option must also be specified to ensure secure connections.
The application context for commands must be loaded unless it is already active, maintaining context across command invocations to ensure stability.
If an error occurs while loading the application, it will propagate immediately unless in a reloading scenario, in which case the error will display while allowing server operation.
The application must be properly initialized before executing any commands that require server operations, such as 'run' or 'shell'.
The loading of environment variables from '.env' or '.flaskenv' files is managed by the 'load_dotenv_defaults' parameter, which defaults to True and can be overridden by the user.
The 'after_this_request' function can only be used when a request context is active, such as inside a route handler.
The 'copy_current_request_context' function can only be used when a request context is active, such as inside a route handler.
Accessing the 'request' property of AppContext raises a RuntimeError if the context does not have an associated request object.
Accessing the 'session' property of AppContext raises a RuntimeError if the context does not have an associated request object.
The push method of AppContext will only perform request matching if the context is not already pushed.
The pop method of AppContext raises a RuntimeError if it is not the active context or if it has been pushed more times than it has been popped.
The has_request_context function returns True if a request context is active; otherwise, it returns False.
The has_app_context function returns True if an app context is active; otherwise, it returns False.
The AppContext constructor initializes the app context with the request and session set to None if they are not provided.
The session object is loaded the first time it is accessed, rather than when the context is pushed.
Teardown functions are executed when the context is popped, based on whether the context is a request or app context.
A JSONProvider must implement the :meth:`dumps` and :meth:`loads` methods for serialization and deserialization of JSON data.
Either positional or keyword arguments can be given to the :meth:`response` method, but not both.
If no arguments are given to the :meth:`response` method, ``None`` is serialized.
Response output is in the ``application/json`` mimetype as specified in the response method.
The :meth:`response` method serializes the given arguments as JSON before returning the Response object.
The :meth:`dumps` method must sort keys in any serialized dictionaries if the ``sort_keys`` attribute is set to True.
The ``default`` method must return a valid JSON type or raise a ``TypeError`` if serialization fails on unsupported types.
The :meth:`loads` method must deserialize data from a string or bytes as JSON, returning the resultant Python object.
The ``compact`` attribute controls the formatting of the response output based on its value and the application's debugging mode.
The ``ensure_ascii`` attribute determines whether non-ASCII characters are replaced with escape sequences during JSON serialization.
The :meth:`dumps` method must apply default serialization behaviors defined by the attributes of the JSONProvider, including ``default``, ``ensure_ascii``, and ``sort_keys``.
A file must be opened for writing with UTF-8 encoding to ensure valid JSON is written when using the :meth:`dump` method.
The :meth:`load` method deserializes data read from a file that is opened for reading text or UTF-8 bytes.
If data is of type :class:`date`, it will be serialized to HTTP date format using the ``default`` method during JSON serialization.
Instances of UUID and decimal types are serialized to their string representations using the ``default`` function during JSON serialization.
Instances of dataclasses are converted to dictionaries using ``dataclasses.asdict`` during serialization.
A session is permanent if the '_permanent' key is set to True.
A session is not guaranteed to be marked as new, regardless of its creation status.
The modified flag for a session must be set to True whenever session data is changed, including changes to mutable data.
The accessed flag indicates whether the session has been accessed, even if it has not been modified. It is set when the session object is accessed through the request context.
A Set-Cookie header should be set for the session cookie if the session is modified or if the session is marked as permanent and SESSION_REFRESH_EACH_REQUEST is set to True.
A null session will be generated when the open_session method fails or returns None, allowing read-only access with an error on modifications.
The name of the session cookie is obtained from app.config['SESSION_COOKIE_NAME'].
The domain for the session cookie is determined by app.config['SESSION_COOKIE_DOMAIN'].
The path for the session cookie is determined by app.config['SESSION_COOKIE_PATH']. If it is not set, it falls back to the value of app.config['APPLICATION_ROOT'].
The HttpOnly attribute status of the session cookie is determined by app.config['SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY'].
The secure attribute status of the session cookie is determined by app.config['SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE'].
The SameSite attribute for the session cookie is determined by app.config['SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE'].
The partitioned attribute of the session cookie is determined by app.config['SESSION_COOKIE_PARTITIONED'].
The expiration time of the session is calculated based on whether the session is permanent and the app's configured permanent_session_lifetime.
If the session is empty and it has been modified, the corresponding cookie should be removed from the response.
A cookie will only be set for the session if the session is not empty and is either modified or has SESSION_REFRESH_EACH_REQUEST enabled.
Signals are created for various stages of a Flask application lifecycle to facilitate communication within the application.
The signal 'template-rendered' indicates a template has been successfully rendered.
The signal 'before-render-template' indicates that a template is about to be rendered.
The signal 'request-started' indicates that the processing of a request has begun.
The signal 'request-finished' indicates that the processing of a request has completed successfully.
The signal 'request-tearing-down' indicates that the request context is being torn down, allowing cleanup operations.
The signal 'got-request-exception' indicates that an exception occurred during the processing of a request.
The signal 'appcontext-tearing-down' indicates that the application context is being destroyed, triggering any cleanup routines.
The signal 'appcontext-pushed' indicates that a new application context has been pushed onto the context stack.
The signal 'appcontext-popped' indicates that the top application context has been removed from the context stack.
The signal 'message-flashed' indicates that a message has been flashed to the user, typically for notifications.
The base_url must be absent, or if provided, it must not coexist with subdomain or url_scheme.
If base_url is None, it is constructed from the server name and application root.
If subdomain is provided, it prepends the server name with the format '{subdomain}.{server_name}'.
If url_scheme is None, it defaults to the application's preferred URL scheme.
The REMOTE_ADDR in the environment base is set to '127.0.0.1'.
The HTTP_USER_AGENT in the environment base is set to the Werkzeug version string.
A session transaction can be initiated using a with statement that modifies the session being used.
Cookies must be enabled for session transactions to proceed; otherwise, a TypeError is raised.
If the session backend fails to open a session, a RuntimeError is raised.
The invoke method for FlaskCliRunner defaults to the application's CLI group if no CLI command is provided.
If 'obj' is not provided in the kwargs when invoking a CLI command, a ScriptInfo instance is automatically passed to it.
